claim: The Xrcc4M61R mouse line was developed through CRISPR/Cas9 to overcome the embryonic lethality of Xrcc4-deficient mice.
source: We developed an Xrcc4M61R separation of function mouse line to overcome the embryonic lethality of Xrcc4-deficient mice.
evidence: The abstract directly states the development of the mouse line and its purpose.

claim: XRCC4M61R protein does not interact with Xlf.
source: XRCC4M61R protein does not interact with Xlf, thus obliterating XRCC4-Xlf filament formation while preserving the ability to stabilize DNA ligase IV.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the loss of interaction between XRCC4M61R and Xlf.

claim: XRCC4M61R protein preserves the ability to stabilize DNA ligase IV.
source: XRCC4M61R protein does not interact with Xlf, thus obliterating XRCC4-Xlf filament formation while preserving the ability to stabilize DNA ligase IV.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that XRCC4M61R retains Lig4 stabilization function.

claim: X4M61R mice are DNA repair deficient.
source: X4M61R mice, which are DNA repair deficient, phenocopy the Nhej1-/- (known as Xlf -/-) setting with a minor impact on the development of the adaptive immune system.
evidence: The abstract directly states the DNA repair deficiency of X4M61R mice.

claim: X4M61R mice phenocopy the Nhej1-/- (Xlf-/-) setting with a minor impact on the development of the adaptive immune system.
source: X4M61R mice, which are DNA repair deficient, phenocopy the Nhej1-/- (known as Xlf -/-) setting with a minor impact on the development of the adaptive immune system.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the phenotypic similarity between X4M61R and Nhej1-/- mice.

claim: The core NHEJ DNA repair factor XRCC4 is not mandatory for V(D)J recombination aside from its role in stabilizing DNA ligase IV.
source: The core non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ) DNA repair factor XRCC4 is therefore not mandatory for V(D)J recombination aside from its role in stabilizing DNA ligase IV.
evidence: The abstract explicitly concludes that XRCC4 is not essential for V(D)J recombination beyond Lig4 stabilization.

claim: Xrcc4M61R mice crossed on Paxx-/- background are severely immunocompromised owing to aborted V(D)J recombination.
source: In contrast, Xrcc4M61R mice crossed on Paxx-/-, Nhej1-/-, or Atm-/- backgrounds are severely immunocompromised, owing to aborted V(D)J recombination as in Xlf-Paxx and Xlf-Atm double Knock Out (DKO) settings.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the severe immunocompromised phenotype of Xrcc4M61R-Paxx double mutants.

claim: Xrcc4M61R mice crossed on Nhej1-/- background are severely immunocompromised owing to aborted V(D)J recombination.
source: In contrast, Xrcc4M61R mice crossed on Paxx-/-, Nhej1-/-, or Atm-/- backgrounds are severely immunocompromised, owing to aborted V(D)J recombination as in Xlf-Paxx and Xlf-Atm double Knock Out (DKO) settings.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the severe immunocompromised phenotype of Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1 double mutants.

claim: Xrcc4M61R mice crossed on Atm-/- background are severely immunocompromised owing to aborted V(D)J recombination.
source: In contrast, Xrcc4M61R mice crossed on Paxx-/-, Nhej1-/-, or Atm-/- backgrounds are severely immunocompromised, owing to aborted V(D)J recombination as in Xlf-Paxx and Xlf-Atm double Knock Out (DKO) settings.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the severe immunocompromised phenotype of Xrcc4M61R-Atm double mutants.

claim: Massive apoptosis of post-mitotic neurons causes embryonic lethality of Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1-/- double mutants.
source: Furthermore, massive apoptosis of post-mitotic neurons causes embryonic lethality of Xrcc4M61R -Nhej1-/- double mutants.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the cause of embryonic lethality in double mutants.

claim: V(D)J recombination results in the somatic rearrangement of variable (V), diversity (D), and joining (J) elements of antigen receptor loci in T- and B-cell precursors.
source: V(D)J recombination results in the somatic rearrangement of variable (V), diversity (D), and joining (J) elements of antigen receptor loci in T- and B-cell precursors (Jung et al., 2006).
evidence: The introduction explicitly describes V(D)J recombination with a citation to support the statement.

claim: V(D)J recombination is initiated by the domesticated transposase Recombination-Activating Genes 1 and 2 factors (RAG1/2).
source: It is initiated by the domesticated transposase Recombination-Activating Genes 1 and 2 factors (RAG1/2), which introduce prDSBs at the border of V, D, and J elements within recombination signal sequences (RSS).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states that RAG1/2 initiates V(D)J recombination.

claim: The NHEJ machinery is the sole DNA repair pathway to cope with lymphoid-specific prDSBs.
source: The non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ) machinery is the sole DNA repair pathway to cope with these lymphoid-specific prDSBs.
evidence: The introduction explicitly states that NHEJ is the only pathway for repairing prDSBs during V(D)J recombination.

claim: The NHEJ pathway is signaled by the Ataxia-Telangiectasia mutated (ATM) protein.
source: Briefly, the NHEJ pathway is signaled by the Ataxia-Telangiectasia mutated (ATM) protein (Arya and Bassing, 2017; Bassing et al., 2002)
evidence: The introduction explicitly states ATM's role in signaling NHEJ with supporting citations.

claim: The Ku70-Ku80 complex recognizes broken DNA ends and recruits DNA-PKcs.
source: and prompted by the Ku70-Ku80 complex that recognizes broken DNA ends and recruits the DNA-dependent protein kinase-catalytic subunit (DNA-PKcs), which further activates the pathway (Sibanda et al., 2017).
evidence: The introduction explicitly describes the role of Ku70-Ku80 complex with a supporting citation.

claim: Artemis endo/exonuclease specifically opens the RAG1/2-generated hairpins at DNA ends during V(D)J recombination.
source: Broken DNA ends are processed by Artemis endo/exonuclease, which specifically opens the RAG1/2-generated hairpins at DNA ends during V(D)J recombination (Chang et al., 2017).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states Artemis's function with a supporting citation.

claim: DNA ligase IV (Lig4), XRCC4, Xlf, and PAXX ensure ligation of broken ends.
source: DNA ligase IV (Lig4), X-ray repair cross-complementation 4 (XRCC4, or X4), XRCC4-like factor (Xlf, also known as Cernunnos), and Paralog of XRCC4 and Xlf (PAXX) (Craxton et al., 2015; Ochi et al., 2015; Xing et al., 2015) ensure ligation of broken ends (Lieber, 2010).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the role of these factors in DNA ligation with supporting citations.

claim: Both Lig4-/- and Xrcc4-/- mice suffer late embryonic lethality caused by apoptosis of post-mitotic neurons.
source: Lig4 and XRCC4 are critical factors during development apart from their essential function during V(D)J recombination, and both Lig4-/- and Xrcc4-/- mice suffer late embryonic lethality caused by apoptosis of post-mitotic neurons (Barnes et al., 1998; Frank et al., 1998; Shull et al., 2009).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the embryonic lethality phenotype with supporting citations.

claim: Human patients with LIG4 syndrome present with dwarfism, microcephaly, and various degrees of immunodeficiency caused by hypomorphic mutations in the Lig4 gene.
source: Likewise, human patients with LIG4 syndrome present with dwarfism, microcephaly, and various degrees of immunodeficiency caused by hypomorphic mutations in the Lig4 gene (O'Driscoll et al., 2001; Staines Boone et al., 2018).
evidence: The introduction explicitly describes LIG4 syndrome phenotypes with supporting citations.

claim: Defects in core NHEJ factors result in severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) owing to aborted V(D)J recombination both in humans and animal models.
source: In most of the cases, defects in core NHEJ factors result in severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID), owing to aborted V(D)J recombination both in humans and animal models (de Villartay et al., 2003).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the consequence of NHEJ defects with a supporting citation.

claim: NHEJ deficiency results in genetic instability with the development of Pro-B cell lymphomas harboring chromosomal translocations when associated with Trp53-/-.
source: NHEJ deficiency also results in genetic instability with the development of Pro-B cell lymphomas harboring chromosomal translocations when associated with Trp53-/- (Alt et al., 2013).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the consequence of NHEJ deficiency in Trp53-/- background with a supporting citation.

claim: Xlf/Cernunnos-deficient patients present with developmental features including dwarfism, microcephaly, and combined immunodeficiency (CID).
source: Xlf/Cernunnos-deficient patients also present with developmental features including dwarfism, microcephaly, and combined immunodeficiency (CID) (Buck et al., 2006).
evidence: The introduction explicitly describes Xlf-deficient patient phenotypes with a supporting citation.

claim: V(D)J recombination is not severely affected in human Xlf deficiency.
source: However, V(D)J recombination is not severely affected nor in human (Buck et al., 2006; Recio et al., 2018; van der Burg and Gennery, 2011) or murine (Li et al., 2008; Roch et al., 2019; Vera et al., 2013) settings of Xlf deficiency.
evidence: The introduction explicitly states that V(D)J recombination is not severely affected in Xlf deficiency with supporting citations.

claim: V(D)J recombination is not severely affected in murine Xlf deficiency.
source: However, V(D)J recombination is not severely affected nor in human (Buck et al., 2006; Recio et al., 2018; van der Burg and Gennery, 2011) or murine (Li et al., 2008; Roch et al., 2019; Vera et al., 2013) settings of Xlf deficiency.
evidence: The introduction explicitly states that V(D)J recombination is not severely affected in Xlf deficiency with supporting citations.

claim: The paradoxical situation of Xlf deficiency is a consequence of the functional redundancy between Xlf and several DNA repair factors, including PAXX, ATM, H2A.X, MDC1, MRI, and 53BP1.
source: This paradoxical situation is a consequence of the functional redundancy between Xlf and several DNA repair factors, including PAXX, ATM, H2A.X, MDC1, MRI, and 53BP1 as revealed by the complete V(D)J recombination defect in combined deficient settings (Abramowski et al., 2018; Beck et al., 2019; Hung et al., 2018; Musilli et al., 2020; Oksenych et al., 2012; Zha et al., 2011)
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the functional redundancy with supporting citations.

claim: RAG2 itself shows functional redundancy with Xlf.
source: This paradoxical situation is a consequence of the functional redundancy between Xlf and several DNA repair factors, including PAXX, ATM, H2A.X, MDC1, MRI, and 53BP1 as revealed by the complete V(D)J recombination defect in combined deficient settings (Abramowski et al., 2018; Beck et al., 2019; Hung et al., 2018; Musilli et al., 2020; Oksenych et al., 2012; Zha et al., 2011) as well as RAG2 itself (Lescale et al., 2016a).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states RAG2's functional redundancy with Xlf with a supporting citation.

claim: Nhej1-Trp53 DKO mice do not develop Pro-B cell lymphomas.
source: Consistent with their overall efficient V(D)J recombination, Nhej1-Trp53 DKO mice indeed do not develop Pro-B cell lymphomas (Vera et al., 2013).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the absence of lymphoma development with a supporting citation.

claim: The C-terminus of RAG2 is determinant in complementing the lack of Xlf.
source: We previously established that the C-terminus of RAG2 is determinant in complementing the lack of Xlf (Lescale et al., 2016a).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the role of RAG2 C-terminus with a supporting citation.

claim: The combined absence of the C-terminus of RAG2 and Xlf results in SCID mice owing to a complete block of V(D)J recombination.
source: Indeed, the combined absence of the C-terminus of RAG2 and Xlf results in SCID mice owing to a complete block of V(D)J recombination.
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the consequence of combined RAG2 C-terminus and Xlf deficiency.

claim: RAG2/Xlf double mutant mice develop typical NHEJ-deficient pro-B cell lymphomas when crossed onto a Trp53-/- background.
source: Indeed, RAG2/Xlf double mutant mice develop typical NHEJ-deficient pro-B cell lymphomas when crossed onto a Trp53-/- background (Lescale et al., 2016a).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the lymphoma development with a supporting citation.

claim: Human patients identified with X4 mutations present DNA repair defect hallmarks, including dwarfism, microcephaly, increased cellular sensitivity to radiomimetic agents, but no immunodeficiency.
source: Reminiscent to the Xlf-deficient condition, human patients identified with X4 mutations present DNA repair defect hallmarks, including dwarfism, microcephaly, increased cellular sensitivity to radiomimetic agents, but, strikingly, no immunodeficiency (de Villartay, 2015; Saito et al., 2016).
evidence: The introduction explicitly describes X4-deficient patient phenotypes with supporting citations.

claim: X4 stabilizes Lig4 through its C-terminal coiled-coil domain.
source: First, X4 stabilizes Lig4 through its C-terminal coiled-coil domain (Grawunder et al., 1997).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the mechanism of Lig4 stabilization with a supporting citation.

claim: Lig4 expression is abrogated in Xrcc4 Knock Out (KO) models both in vivo and in vitro.
source: Indeed, Lig4 expression is abrogated in Xrcc4 Knock Out (KO) models both in vivo and in vitro (Gao et al., 1998).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the consequence of Xrcc4 KO with a supporting citation.

claim: X4 and Xlf homodimers interact through their N-terminal globular head to form long polymeric 'filaments'.
source: In addition, X4 and Xlf homodimers interact through their N-terminal globular head to form long polymeric 'filaments' (Reid et al., 2015; Ropars et al., 2011).
evidence: The introduction explicitly describes the X4-Xlf filament formation with supporting citations.

claim: X4-Xlf filaments generate a 'DNA repair synapse' to tether broken DNA ends.
source: X4-Xlf filaments generate a 'DNA repair synapse' to tether broken DNA ends (Brouwer et al., 2016; Reid et al., 2015).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the function of X4-Xlf filaments with supporting citations.

claim: Xrcc4-/- mice phenocopy Lig4-/- condition, with an embryonic lethality and SCID phenotype.
source: Since X4 is compulsory for Lig4 stabilization, Xrcc4-/- mice phenocopy Lig4-/- condition, with an embryonic lethality and SCID phenotype (Gao et al., 1998).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the phenotype of Xrcc4-/- mice with a supporting citation.

claim: The embryonic lethality of Xrcc4-/- mice is rescued on Trp53-/- background.
source: The embryonic lethality is rescued on Trp53-/- background, but the SCID resulting from a complete block of lymphocyte development remains (Gao et al., 2000).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the rescue of embryonic lethality with a supporting citation.

claim: Xrcc4-/-Trp53-/- DKO mice develop Pro-B cell lymphomas.
source: Furthermore, Xrcc4-/-Trp53-/- DKO mice develop Pro-B cell lymphomas (Chen et al., 2016; Gao et al., 2000).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states the lymphoma development with supporting citations.

claim: The X4M61R substitution abrogates X4-Xlf interaction.
source: X4 and Xlf interact through a hydrophobic interface, which is disrupted by the X4M61R substitution, thus resulting in the loss of X4-Xlf filament (Ropars et al., 2011).
evidence: The Results section explicitly states the effect of M61R substitution with a supporting citation.

claim: Homozygous Xrcc4M61R/M61R mice were viable.
source: Homozygous Xrcc4M61R/M61R mice (Xrcc4M61R mice) were viable arguing against any harmful impact of the M61R substitution during embryonic development, as opposed to the embryonic lethality of Xrcc4 KOs.
evidence: The Results section explicitly states the viability of Xrcc4M61R mice.

claim: RT-PCR analysis of X4 mRNA expression unveiled two isoforms in M61R mutation-bearing cells.
source: RT-PCR analysis of X4 mRNA expression unveiled two isoforms in M61R mutation-bearing cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: The Results section explicitly states the RT-PCR findings with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The expression of the full-length transcript carrying the five mutations was reduced.
source: The expression of the full-length transcript carrying the five mutations was reduced (Figure 1B, upper band) and was accompanied by a shorter isoform (Figure 1B, lower band).
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the transcript expression pattern with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Sequencing the alternative transcript revealed the out-of-frame splicing-out of exon 3.
source: Sequencing this alternative transcript revealed the out-of-frame splicing-out of exon 3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The Results section explicitly states the sequencing results with reference to a figure supplement.

claim: X4 expression was barely detectable in spleen, brain, thymus, and MEFs from Xrcc4M61R mice.
source: At the protein level, X4 expression was barely detectable in spleen, brain, thymus, and mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) from Xrcc4M61R mice as opposed to their homozygous WT counterparts (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the protein expression with reference to Figures 1C and D.

claim: Lig4 protein was readily detectable by WB in protein lysates from Xrcc4M61R mice spleen and thymus.
source: Of note, Lig4 protein was readily detectable by WB in protein lysates from Xrcc4M61R mice spleen and thymus, attesting for its stabilization by the X4M61R protein (Figure 1E).
evidence: The Results section explicitly states the Lig4 detection with reference to Figure 1E.

claim: MEFs from Xrcc4M61R mice presented a statistically significant decrease in cell viability compared to WT cells upon phleomycin treatment.
source: MEFs from Xrcc4M61R mice presented a statistically significant decrease in cell viability compared to WT cells upon phleomycin, a DSB inducer, treatment, attesting for a profound DNA repair defect (Figure 1F).
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the phleomycin sensitivity with reference to Figure 1F.

claim: Splenic T cells from Xrcc4M61R mice showed an increased IR sensitivity with an almost complete loss of viability at 2 Gy.
source: Likewise, splenic T cells from Xrcc4M61R mice showed an increased IR sensitivity with an almost complete loss of viability at 2 Gy (Figure 1G).
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the IR sensitivity with reference to Figure 1G.

claim: Thymocyte counts were significantly reduced in Xrcc4M61R thymus.
source: Thymocyte counts were significantly reduced in Xrcc4M61R thymus (Figure 2A), but remained in the range of Nhej1-/- thymus cellularity (respectively [*106] 26.8 ± 2.6 SEM vs. 115 ± 15 SEM in WT, p<0.0001, vs. 12.5 ± 2.6 SEM in Nhej1-/-, ns).
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the thymocyte counts with reference to Figure 2A and statistical analysis.

claim: Xrcc4M61R thymocytes presented a mild accumulation of CD44-CD25+ CD28- DN3A thymocytes.
source: The thymocyte maturation program, identified through the various CD4/CD8 stages, was similar in Xrcc4M61R and WT littermates (Figure 2B), yet with a mild accumulation of CD44-CD25+ CD28- DN3A Xrcc4M61R thymocytes (respectively 81.8% ± 0.9 SEM vs. 76.1% ± 0.7 SEM, p<0.0001) (Figure 2C)
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the DN3A accumulation with reference to Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: Purified Xrcc4M61R thymocytes presented an increased apoptosis (7AAD+/AnnV+), similar to that of Nhej1-/- thymocytes.
source: Purified Xrcc4M61R thymocytes presented an increased apoptosis (7AAD+/AnnV+), similar to that of Nhej1-/- thymocytes (respectively 47.4% ± 1.7 SEM vs. 33.2% ± 1.3 SEM for WT, p=0.0003, vs. 59.5% ± 1.6 SEM, for Nhej1-/-, ns) (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the apoptosis with reference to Figures 2D and E.

claim: Increased apoptosis in Xrcc4M61R thymocytes was accompanied by the expression of TP53 target genes Cdkn1a, Bbc3, and Bax.
source: This was accompanied by the expression of TP53 target genes Cdkn1a, Bbc3, and Bax, in both Xrcc4M61R and Nhej1-/- thymocytes (Figure 2F).
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the gene expression with reference to Figure 2F.

claim: TCRα repertoire was skewed in Xrcc4M61R thymocytes, with the decreased usage of distal VαJα rearrangements.
source: Lastly, TCRα repertoire was skewed in Xrcc4M61R thymocytes (Figure 2G), with the decreased usage of distal VαJα rearrangements, a hallmark of reduced thymocyte viability or suboptimal V(D)J recombination.
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the TCRα repertoire with reference to Figure 2G.

claim: The proportion of mature B lymphocytes in the bone marrow was not significantly altered in Xrcc4M61R mice.
source: The proportion of mature B lymphocytes in the bone marrow (BM) was not significantly altered in Xrcc4M61R mice (Figure 2H, I), while significantly decreased in Nhej1-/- mice (respectively 21.7% ± 1.8 SEM vs. 26.0% ± 1.1 SEM, ns, vs. 13.3% ± 0.6 SEM, p=.008).
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the B cell proportions with reference to Figures 2H and I.

claim: The proportions of immature B cells were decreased in Xrcc4M61R mice.
source: However, the proportions of immature B cells were decreased in Xrcc4M61R mice (Figure 2J), close to the already described decline of Nhej1-/- immature B cells (respectively 11.3% ± 3.3 SEM vs. 19.3% ± 2.6 SEM, p=0.0002, vs. 8.7% ± 2.5 SEM, ns).
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the immature B cell proportions with reference to Figure 2J.

claim: The thymus and spleen cellularity was severely reduced in both X4M61R-Paxx and Xrcc4M61R-Atm mice.
source: The thymus and spleen cellularity was severely reduced in both X4M61R-Paxx and Xrcc4M61R-Atm mice (Figure 3A and B) as compared to their Xrcc4M61R single-mutant littermates (respectively [*106] 1.1 ± 0.2 SEM and 0.56 ± 0.15 SEM, p<0.0001, vs. 26.8 ± 2.6 SEM in thymus and 6.8 ± 1.2 SEM and 4.1 ± 1.0 SEM, p<0.0001, vs. 40.0 ± 3.8 SEM in spleen)
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the cellularity with reference to Figures 3A and B.

claim: B cells expressing IgM were undetectable in BM from Xrcc4M61R-Atm mice.
source: B cells expressing IgM were undetectable in BM from Xrcc4M61R-Atm mice and to a lesser extent in Xrcc4M61R-Paxx mice (Figure 3C).
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the IgM expression with reference to Figure 3C.

claim: B220+ B cells were strongly reduced compared to Xrcc4M61R or WT littermates in both Xrcc4M61R-Paxx and Xrcc4M61R-Atm settings.
source: B220+ B cells were strongly reduced compared to Xrcc4M61R or WT littermates in both settings (respectively 10.9% ± 1.4 SEM and 7.2% ± 0.96 SEM, p=0.001, vs. 21.7 ± 1.79 SEM in Xrcc4M61R and 26.3 ± 1.08 SEM in WT) (Figure 3D).
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the B220+ B cell proportions with reference to Figure 3D.

claim: Xrcc4M61R-Paxx and X4M61R-Atm mice presented with a substantial accumulation of DN3A thymocytes.
source: Likewise, Xrcc4M61R-Paxx and X4M61R-Atm mice presented with a substantial accumulation of DN3A thymocytes (93.4% ± 0.8 SEM and 98.2% ± 0.3 SEM, p=0.0001, respectively, vs. 76.1 ± 0.7 SEM in WT), which was significantly greater than the one observed for Xrcc4M61R (81.77 ± 1.4 SEM) or Nhej1-/- (81.1 ± 1.4 SEM) animals (Figure 3E and Abramowski et al., 2018).
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the DN3A accumulation with reference to Figure 3E and a citation.

claim: Dβ2-Jβ2 and Vβ10-Dβ2Jβ2 rearrangements of the Tcrb locus were present in thymocytes from Xrcc4M61R, Atm-/-, and WT mice.
source: Indeed, while Dβ2-Jβ2 (upper panel) and Vβ10-Dβ2Jβ2 (lower panel) rearrangements of the Tcrb locus were present in thymocytes from Xrcc4M61R, Atm-/-, and WT mice (Figure 3F and G), as also previously observed in Paxx-/- mice (Abramowski et al., 2018), they were barely detectable in DNA from Xrcc4M61R-Paxx and Xrcc4M61R-Atm thymus.
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the Tcrb rearrangements with reference to Figures 3F and G and a citation.

claim: Dβ2-Jβ2 and Vβ10-Dβ2Jβ2 rearrangements were barely detectable in DNA from Xrcc4M61R-Paxx and Xrcc4M61R-Atm thymus.
source: Indeed, while Dβ2-Jβ2 (upper panel) and Vβ10-Dβ2Jβ2 (lower panel) rearrangements of the Tcrb locus were present in thymocytes from Xrcc4M61R, Atm-/-, and WT mice (Figure 3F and G), as also previously observed in Paxx-/- mice (Abramowski et al., 2018), they were barely detectable in DNA from Xrcc4M61R-Paxx and Xrcc4M61R-Atm thymus.
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the absence of Tcrb rearrangements in double mutants.

claim: No Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1-/- double homozygous mice could be recovered out of 166 newborns obtained from various genotype combinations, when 23 were expected.
source: No Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1-/- double homozygous mice (hereafter named as Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1) could be recovered out of 166 newborns obtained from various genotype combinations, when 23 were expected (Figure 4A), testifying the lethality of Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1 embryos.
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the absence of double mutant mice with reference to Figure 4A.

claim: Lived Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1 fetuses could be recovered at E15.5 and E18.5.
source: Nevertheless, lived Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1 fetuses could be recovered at E15.5 and E18.5.
evidence: The Results section explicitly states the recovery of live fetuses.

claim: Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1 fetuses were smaller than their Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1+/- littermates.
source: They were smaller than their Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1+/- littermates, confirming abnormal development (Figure 4B and data not shown).
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the size difference with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: Massive neuronal apoptosis was detected in E15.5 brain slices through cleaved-caspase 3 (CC3) staining in upper layers of dorsal telencephalon in Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1 mice.
source: Massive neuronal apoptosis was detected in E15.5 brain slices through cleaved-caspase 3 (CC3) staining in upper layers of dorsal telencephalon corresponding to the intermediate zone (IZ) and the cortical plate (CP) in Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1 mice (Figure 4C–E).
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the neuronal apoptosis with reference to Figures 4C-E.

claim: Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1 Pro-B cells failed to express intracellular μH chain when compared to WT.
source: Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1 Pro-B cells failed to express intracellular μH chain when compared to WT (0.90% ± 0.09 SEM, p=0.008), which contrasted with the slight reduction observed in Xrcc4M61R and Nhej1-/- mice (respectively 16.6% ± 1.2 SEM and 19.1% ± 2.2 SEM vs. 32.8% ± 1.3 SEM, p=0.0016) (Figure 5A and B)
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the μH chain expression with reference to Figures 5A and B.

claim: Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1 thymocyte development was severely compromised from the DN3A stage on.
source: In contrast, Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1 thymocyte development was severely compromised from the DN3A stage on when compared to Xrcc4M61R and Nhej1-/- (99.4% ± 0.13 SEM, p=0.0007), and DP thymocytes or mature T cells were virtually absent from these thymii (Figure 5A and C).
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the thymocyte development with reference to Figures 5A and C.

claim: Dβ2-Jβ2 and Vβ10-Dβ2Jβ2 Tcrb genes rearrangements were undetectable in Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1 thymus.
source: Dβ2-Jβ2 and Vβ10-Dβ2Jβ2 Tcrb genes rearrangements, which begin at around E13 (Ramond et al., 2014), were undetectable in Xrcc4M61R-Nhej1 thymus, while readily observed in WT, Xrcc4M61R, and Nhej1-/- mice (Figure 5D and E)
evidence: The Results section explicitly describes the absence of Tcrb rearrangements with reference to Figures 5D and E and a citation.

claim: The embryonic lethality of Xrcc4 KO mice is most likely the result of the de facto absence of Lig4 in this setting.
source: The X4M61R protein, although weakly expressed, preserves the stabilization of Lig4 but severely compromises the NHEJ DNA repair function in affected mice. Nevertheless, Xrcc4M61R mice are viable, arguing that the embryonic lethality of Xrcc4 KO mice is most likely the result of the de facto absence of Lig4 in this setting, thus phenocopying Lig4 KO condition.
evidence: The Discussion section explicitly states the interpretation of the embryonic lethality.

claim: The formation of the X4-Xlf filament is dispensable for post-mitotic neuron viability.
source: Interestingly, this also indicates that the formation of the X4-Xlf filament, abrogated by the M61R mutation, is dispensable for post-mitotic neuron viability, the loss of which causes lethality in Xrcc4 and Lig4 KO settings.
evidence: The Discussion section explicitly states the interpretation regarding X4-Xlf filament and neuron viability.

claim: X4 is required for V(D)J recombination through Lig4 stabilization.
source: Therefore, although X4 is required for V(D)J recombination through Lig4 stabilization, it is not mandatory for coding-ends tethering during V(D)J recombination.
evidence: The Discussion section explicitly states the role of X4 in V(D)J recombination.

claim: X4 is not mandatory for coding-ends tethering during V(D)J recombination.
